questions.question: If sin A - cos A = frac{sqrt{3} - sqrt{2}}{2}, then the value of sin A. cos A is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If sin A − cos A = x, then sin A × cos A = (1 − x²) ÷ 2.

Here, x = (√3 − √2) / 2

⇒ x² = (3 + 2 − 2√6) / 4 = (5 − 2√6) / 4

⇒ 1 − x² = 1 − [(5 − 2√6) / 4] = (2√6 − 1) / 4

⇒ sin A × cos A = [(2√6 − 1) / 4] ÷ 2 = (2√6 − 1) / 8

**∴ The correct answer is (2√6 − 1) / 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A − cos A = (√3 − √2) / 2

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

sin² A + cos² A = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (sin A − cos A)² = [(√3 − √2) / 2]²

⇒ sin² A + cos² A − 2 × sin A × cos A = (3 + 2 − 2√6) / 4

⇒ 1 − 2 × sin A × cos A = (5 − 2√6) / 4

⇒ 2 × sin A × cos A = 1 − [(5 − 2√6) / 4]

⇒ 2 × sin A × cos A = (4 − 5 + 2√6) / 4

⇒ 2 × sin A × cos A = (2√6 − 1) / 4

⇒ sin A × cos A = (2√6 − 1) / 8

**∴ The correct answer is (2√6 − 1) / 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

Double Angle Formulas

sin(2θ) = 2 × sin θ × cos θ and cos(2θ) = cos² θ − sin² θ.

Sum and Difference Relations

If sin θ + cos θ = p, then squaring gives 1 + 2 × sin θ × cos θ = p², which helps in directly calculating the product of sine and cosine.
</p

questions.question:
The following bar chart shows the year-wise percentage hike in the fuel price with respect to the previous year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfdfefb7f68f5047c3735b0f1cd1fc866c0a2ec570bbbfc07fc8f8215b0e2808.png] 

In how many years did the fuel prices NOT rise?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The bar chart shows the year-wise percentage hike in fuel prices for the years 2015 to 2021.

We need to determine how many years the fuel prices did not rise (fuel price hike = 0%).

**Formula used:**

If fuel price hike (%) = 0, it indicates no rise in fuel prices for that year.

**Calculations:**

From the chart:

1. In 2015: Fuel price hike = 8% (prices rose).

2. In 2016: Fuel price hike = 10.5% (prices rose).

3. In 2017: Fuel price hike = 6% (prices rose).

4. In 2018: Fuel price hike = 7% (prices rose).

5. In 2019: Fuel price hike = 8% (prices rose).

6. In 2020: Fuel price hike = 10% (prices rose).

7. In 2021: Fuel price hike = 11% (prices rose).

Observation: In all years from 2015 to 2021, the fuel price hike was greater than 0%.

**∴ The number of years the fuel prices did NOT rise is 0.**

questions.question: The least number which must be subtracted from 7278745 so as to obtain a sum that is divisible by 11 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the divisibility rule of 11, find the difference between the sum of alternate digits.

Sum of digits at odd places = 7 + 7 + 7 + 5 = 26

Sum of digits at even places = 2 + 8 + 4 = 14

Difference = 26 − 14 = 12

The remainder when 12 is divided by 11 is 1, so we must subtract 1 from the number.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 7278745

Divisor = 11

**Formula Used:**

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us divide the given number 7278745 by 11 using long division.

⇒ 7278745 = (11 × 661704) + 1

⇒ Quotient = 661704

⇒ Remainder = 1

⇒ To make the number exactly divisible by 11, we must subtract the remainder from the dividend.

⇒ 7278745 − 1 = 7278744 (which is perfectly divisible by 11)

⇒ Thus, the least number to be subtracted is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the total sum of its digits is exactly divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 7

Double the last digit of the number and subtract it from the remaining truncated part. If the result is divisible by 7, the original number is also divisible by 7.

Remainder Theorem Application

The remainder obtained upon dividing a number is always the least positive value that must be subtracted from the dividend to make it a perfect multiple of the divisor.
</p

questions.question: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal distance upstream and downstream, Total Time = [Distance × (2 × Speed of Boat)] ÷ (Speed of Boat² − Stream Speed²)

⇒ 7.5 = [50 × (2 × 15)] ÷ (15² − s²)

⇒ 7.5 = 1500 ÷ (225 − s²)

⇒ 225 − s² = 200 ⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the motorboat in still water (v) = 15 km/h

Distance covered in each direction (D) = 50 km

Total time taken (T) = 7 hours 30 minutes = 7.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = v + s

Upstream Speed = v − s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90d7d394c756d0fc671f442f987c0cb89eb4edd7960a13bb347a629a5b6a8a95.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.

⇒ Time taken downstream = 50 ÷ (15 + s)

⇒ Time taken upstream = 50 ÷ (15 − s)

Since the total time is 7.5 hours:

⇒ [50 ÷ (15 + s)] + [50 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

Taking 50 common from the numerator:

⇒ 50 × [1 ÷ (15 + s) + 1 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [(15 − s + 15 + s) ÷ (15 + s)(15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [30 ÷ (225 − s²)] = 7.5

⇒ 1500 ÷ (225 − s²) = 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 1500 ÷ 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 200

⇒ s² = 225 − 200

⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

When going downstream and returning upstream over the same distance, Average speed = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a room is 15 m, 9 m, and 5 m, respectively. From each can of paint 40 square metre of area is painted. How many cans of paint will be needed to paint only the walls of the room?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of walls (Lateral Surface Area) = 2 × (L + B) × H

⇒ Area to paint = 2 × (15 + 9) × 5 = 240 m²

Number of cans = Total Area ÷ Area covered per can

⇒ Cans needed = 240 ÷ 40 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cans.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c648f91a6b9d03bf0787017ac624f18cddb92a99fc49dc4f137550b77693ec60.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the room (L) = 15 m

Breadth of the room (B) = 9 m

Height of the room (H) = 5 m

Area painted by 1 can = 40 m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of 4 walls (Lateral Surface Area of Cuboid) = 2 × (L + B) × H

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Area of walls = 2 × (15 + 9) × 5

⇒ Total Area of walls = 2 × 24 × 5

⇒ Total Area of walls = 48 × 5

⇒ Total Area of walls = 240 m²

⇒ Number of cans needed = Total Area ÷ Area covered by 1 can

⇒ Number of cans needed = 240 ÷ 40

⇒ Number of cans needed = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cans.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

The total surface area covers all 6 faces (walls, floor, and ceiling) of the cuboid. It is given by the formula: TSA = 2 × (L×B + B×H + H×L).

Area of Walls and Ceiling

When painting a room including the ceiling but excluding the floor, the area formula used is: Area = 2 × (L + B) × H + L × B.

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the cuboid inside is given by the product of its three dimensions: Volume = L × B × H.
</p

questions.question: The distance between the longest chord and the centre of a circle is:

options.text: equal to the half of the radius

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The longest chord of any circle is its diameter.

By definition, the diameter always passes exactly through the centre of the circle.

Therefore, the perpendicular distance from the centre to the longest chord is exactly zero.

**∴ The correct answer is 0 unit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
 
 O (Centre)
 A
 B
 Longest Chord AB = Diameter

**Given:**

A circle with its longest chord.

**Concept Used:**

A chord is a line segment whose endpoints lie on the circumference of the circle.

The length of a chord increases as its perpendicular distance from the centre decreases.

The longest possible chord in any circle is its diameter.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the centre of the given circle be O.

⇒ Let AB be the longest chord of the circle.

⇒ Since AB is the longest chord, it must be the diameter.

⇒ The diameter passes directly through the centre point O.

⇒ The perpendicular distance from a point to a line passing through that same point is zero.

⇒ Hence, the distance between the longest chord and the centre of the circle is 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0 unit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chord of a Circle

A line segment connecting any two points on the circumference of a circle is called a chord. The perpendicular line drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Distance and Chord Length Relationship

Chords that are equidistant from the centre are equal in length. As a chord gets closer to the centre, its length increases proportionally.

Diameter

The diameter is a special chord that passes entirely through the centre. It represents the maximum width of the circle and its length is equal to twice the radius (d = 2 × r).
</p

questions.question: The marked price of 55 items was equal to the cost price of 99 items. The selling price of 56 items was equal to the marked price of 35 items. Calculate the profit or loss percentage from the sale of each item.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Write the given conditions as direct price ratios: MP / CP = 99 / 55 = 9 / 5 and SP / MP = 35 / 56 = 5 / 8

Multiply the ratios to find the direct relation between Selling Price and Cost Price:

(SP / MP) × (MP / CP) = (5 / 8) × (9 / 5) ⇒ SP / CP = 45 / 40 = 9 / 8

Since SP = 9 and CP = 8, Profit = 9 − 8 = 1 unit.

Profit % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price of 55 items = Cost Price of 99 items

Selling Price of 56 items = Marked Price of 35 items

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30a3dd5b2504988628f28ca338e1b0ddf382c8570088e57fa30c9f0aa5acb30a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 55 × MP = 99 × CP

⇒ MP / CP = 99 / 55 = 9 / 5

⇒ 56 × SP = 35 × MP

⇒ SP / MP = 35 / 56 = 5 / 8

To equalize the ratio parts of Marked Price, take the LCM of 9 and 8, which is 72.

⇒ MP = 72 units

⇒ CP = (5 / 9) × 72 = 40 units

⇒ SP = (5 / 8) × 72 = 45 units

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 45 − 40 = 5 units

⇒ Profit % = (5 ÷ 40) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the effective single discount is: (x + y − xy / 100)%.

Profit & Loss Relation

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise.
</p

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, P received 42% of the valid votes and Q won by 45,360 votes. 20% people did not cast their vote. If 10% of the votes cast were found invalid, what is the total number of votes registered in the poll booth?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total registered votes be V.

Valid votes = V × 0.80 (cast) × 0.90 (valid) = 0.72V

Q's winning margin = (100% − 42%) − 42% = 16% of valid votes.

Margin = 0.16 × 0.72V = 0.1152V

0.1152V = 45,360 ⇒ V = 3,93,750

**∴ The correct answer is 3,93,750 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Votes not cast = 20%

Invalid votes = 10% of cast votes

P's vote share = 42% of valid votes

Winning margin = 45,360 votes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3f97c3db787e3b7297df083b23c643ac85c9b1cf33f59c7a8621791293673dc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of registered voters be 100x.

⇒ Number of votes cast = 100x − 20% of 100x = 80x

⇒ Valid votes = 80x − 10% of 80x = 72x

⇒ Votes received by P = 42% of 72x = 30.24x

⇒ Votes received by Q = (100% − 42%) = 58% of 72x = 41.76x

⇒ Q's winning margin = 41.76x − 30.24x = 11.52x

⇒ 11.52x = 45,360

⇒ x = 45,360 ÷ 11.52 = 3937.5

⇒ Total registered voters = 100x = 100 × 3937.5 = 3,93,750

**∴ The correct answer is 3,93,750 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid & Invalid Votes

Invalid votes are calculated only on the total votes cast. Votes not cast are excluded before checking validity.
Formula: Valid Votes = Total Votes Cast − Invalid Votes.

Successive Percentage Change

Election problems often involve successive percentage deductions. The multiplying factor method is fastest.
Formula: Final Value = Base × (1 − a%) × (1 − b%).

Winning Margin

Margin of victory is the difference in votes between the winner and the nearest rival.
Formula: Margin = (Winner % − Loser %) of Valid Votes.
</p

questions.question: Hema is 20 years old and her sister Neha is 30 years old. How many years ago were their ages in the ratio of 3 : 5?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age difference is always constant. Difference between Hema and Neha = 30 − 20 = 10 years.

The past ratio is 3 : 5. Difference in ratio parts = 5 − 3 = 2 parts.

2 parts = 10 years ⇒ 1 part = 5 years.

Hema's age at that time = 3 × 5 = 15 years.

Years ago = Present age − Past age = 20 − 15 = 5 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present age of Hema = 20 years

Present age of Neha = 30 years

Ratio of their ages x years ago = 3 : 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71c4be6b761e750403324d70e586ba512dd255c94fdae28f396b1e70c89765eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required number of years be x.

⇒ Hema's age x years ago = 20 − x

⇒ Neha's age x years ago = 30 − x

⇒ According to the given ratio condition: (20 − x) / (30 − x) = 3 / 5

⇒ Cross-multiplying the equation:

⇒ 5 × (20 − x) = 3 × (30 − x)

⇒ 100 − 5x = 90 − 3x

⇒ 5x − 3x = 100 − 90

⇒ 2x = 10

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two individuals is constant and remains exactly the same throughout their lives.

Time Shifting in Ages

If the current age of a person is P, their age t years ago is expressed as (P − t), and their age t years in the future is expressed as (P + t).

Cross-Multiplication Rule

When solving direct proportions or age ratios of the form a / b = c / d, the most efficient method is cross-multiplication, resulting in a × d = b × c.
</p

questions.question: XAB and XCD are two secants to a circle. If XA = 18 cm, AB = 22 cm and XC = 24 cm, then find the value of XD (in cm).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the secant intersection theorem, XA × XB = XC × XD.

The total length of the first secant is XB = XA + AB = 18 + 22 = 40 cm.

Substitute the values directly into the formula: 18 × 40 = 24 × XD

⇒ 720 = 24 × XD ⇒ XD = 30 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of external segment XA = 18 cm

Length of internal segment AB = 22 cm

Length of external segment XC = 24 cm

**Formula Used:**

When two secant lines intersect at a point outside a circle, the product of the external segment and the total secant length is constant for both lines.

⇒ XA × XB = XC × XD

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 X
 
 
 A
 
 
 B
 
 
 C
 
 
 D

 18 cm
 22 cm
 24 cm
 Find XD = ?

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of secant XB = XA + AB

⇒ XB = 18 + 22 = 40 cm

⇒ According to the secant theorem: XA × XB = XC × XD

⇒ 18 × 40 = 24 × XD

⇒ 720 = 24 × XD

⇒ XD = 720 ÷ 24

⇒ XD = 30 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Secant Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, the square of the tangent segment equals the product of the secant's external segment and its total length. Formula: PT² = PA × PB.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

If two chords intersect inside a circle, the product of the segments of one chord is equal to the product of the segments of the other chord. Formula: AE × EB = CE × ED.

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of a direct common tangent to two circles with radii r₁ and r₂, and distance d between their centers is given by: DCT = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).
</p

questions.question: If cos A + cos²A = 1 then sin²A + sin⁴A is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

From cos A + cos²A = 1, we directly get cos A = 1 − cos²A = sin²A.

Squaring both sides gives cos²A = sin⁴A.

Substitute these into the required expression: sin²A + sin⁴A.

This transforms into cos A + cos²A, which is already given as 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cos A + cos²A = 1

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ cos A + cos²A = 1

⇒ cos A = 1 − cos²A

⇒ cos A = sin²A

Now, evaluating the required expression:

⇒ sin²A + sin⁴A

⇒ sin²A + (sin²A)²

Substituting sin²A = cos A into the above expression:

⇒ cos A + (cos A)²

⇒ cos A + cos²A

Since it is already given that cos A + cos²A = 1:

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 ⇒ sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ and cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ.

Secant and Tangent Identity

2. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 ⇒ sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ.

Cosecant and Cotangent Identity

3. cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 ⇒ cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ.

Symmetric Pattern Result

If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, then the symmetric expression evaluates to cos²θ + cos⁴θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: Find the fourth proportional to 4, 9 and 16.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c, then x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Here, a = 4, b = 9, and c = 16.

x = (9 × 16) ÷ 4

x = 144 ÷ 4 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e0d6bce24d3ff54692c7f3fe66c0618ee707d326dfa2ff2aad3598f022df7235.png] 

**Given:**

Three numbers are 4, 9, and 16.

**Formula Used:**

For a proportion a : b :: c : d, Product of Extremes = Product of Means

⇒ a × d = b × c

**Calculations:**

Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 4 : 9 :: 16 : x

⇒ 4 × x = 9 × 16

⇒ 4x = 144

⇒ x = 144 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is called the third proportional. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b). It is the value x such that a : x :: x : b.

Invertendo Property

If four numbers are in proportion such that a : b :: c : d, then by invertendo property, b : a :: d : c.
</p

questions.question: The value of : (1)/(cosec theta - cot theta) - (1)/(sin theta) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 30° in the given expression to solve it directly.

⇒ 1 / (cosec 30° − cot 30°) − 1 / sin 30°

⇒ 1 / (2 − √3) − 2

⇒ Rationalizing the first term: (2 + √3) / (4 − 3) − 2

⇒ 2 + √3 − 2 = √3

Checking the options for θ = 30°, we see that only cot 30° gives √3.

**∴ The correct answer is cot θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

1 / (cosec θ − cot θ) − 1 / sin θ

**Formula Used:**

cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 and 1 / sin θ = cosec θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Multiply the numerator and denominator of the first term by (cosec θ + cot θ)

⇒ Expression = (cosec θ + cot θ) / (cosec²θ − cot²θ) − cosec θ

⇒ Since cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1, the denominator of the first term becomes 1

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ − cosec θ

⇒ cot θ

**∴ The correct answer is cot θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identities

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

2. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 ⇒ 1 / (sec θ − tan θ) = sec θ + tan θ

3. cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 ⇒ 1 / (cosec θ − cot θ) = cosec θ + cot θ

Value Substitution Trick

For trigonometric simplification questions in exams, substitute standard angles like 30° or 60° to evaluate the expression quickly and match the value directly with the options without extensive algebraic solving.
</p

questions.question: Ten chairs and six tables together cost ₹5,140; three chairs and two tables together cost ₹1,635. The cost of 1 chair and 1 table is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let 1 chair = C and 1 table = T.

10C + 6T = 5140

3C + 2T = 1635 ⇒ Multiply by 3 ⇒ 9C + 6T = 4905

Subtracting: C = 5140 − 4905 = 235

2T = 1635 − (3 × 235) = 930 ⇒ T = 465

**∴ The correct answer is ₹700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of 10 chairs and 6 tables = ₹5140

Cost of 3 chairs and 2 tables = ₹1635

**Method Used:**

Solving linear equations using the elimination method.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost of 1 chair be ₹C and 1 table be ₹T

⇒ 10C + 6T = 5140 ... (i)

⇒ 3C + 2T = 1635 ... (ii)

⇒ Multiply equation (ii) by 3:

⇒ 9C + 6T = 4905 ... (iii)

⇒ Subtract equation (iii) from (i):

⇒ (10C + 6T) − (9C + 6T) = 5140 − 4905

⇒ C = 235

⇒ Substitute C = 235 in equation (ii):

⇒ 3 × 235 + 2T = 1635

⇒ 705 + 2T = 1635

⇒ 2T = 1635 − 705

⇒ 2T = 930

⇒ T = 465

⇒ Cost of 1 chair and 1 table = C + T = 235 + 465 = 700

**∴ The correct answer is ₹700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Elimination Method

Make the coefficients of one variable equal by multiplying with a constant, then add or subtract equations to eliminate that variable.

Substitution Method

Express one variable in terms of the other using one equation, then substitute this expression into the other equation to solve.

Consistency of Linear Equations

For a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, a unique solution exists if a₁÷a₂ ≠ b₁÷b₂.

questions.question: If a + b + c = 0, then the value of (a² + b² + 2ab) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given that, a + b + c = 0

⇒ a + b = −c

The expression to find is a perfect square formula.

⇒ (a² + b² + 2ab) = (a + b)²

⇒ (−c)² = c²

**∴ The correct answer is c².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a + b + c = 0

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ a + b + c = 0

⇒ a + b = −c

⇒ Squaring both sides of the equation, we get:

⇒ (a + b)² = (−c)²

⇒ a² + b² + 2ab = c²

**∴ The correct answer is c².**

**__Additional Information__**

Square of a Trinomial

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Standard Algebraic Identities

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab and a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).
</p

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 8 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Sum be 100 units.

Total Simple Interest for 8 years = 3/5 of 100 = 60 units.

Simple Interest for 1 year = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5 units.

Rate of interest per annum = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Sum) × 100 = (7.5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 7.5% = 7(1/2)%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7(1/2)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb0458219620b35aa60338adc28a72336f7b48ad8612c9cbc9b1c0b9a356594e.png] 

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = 3/5 of Sum (P)

Time (T) = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ (3/5)P = (P × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = (8 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = 2R ÷ 25

⇒ 2R = (3 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ 2R = 15

⇒ R = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5

⇒ Rate of interest = 7.5% = 7(1/2)%

**∴ The correct answer is 7(1/2)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Interest calculated solely on the initial principal amount. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on the initial principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Rule of 72

A quick formula used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual fixed interest rate (Years ≈ 72 ÷ R).

SI vs CI Difference

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain sum is given by: Difference = P(R/100)².
</p

questions.question: The marked price of a bed sheet is ₹500. At the time of its sale, two successive discounts of 10% and 5% are available. Find the selling price (in ₹) of the bed sheet.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the successive discount percentages directly into multiplying fractions.

10% discount means selling at 90% ⇒ fraction is 9/10.

5% discount means selling at 95% ⇒ fraction is 19/20.

SP = MP × fraction₁ × fraction₂

SP = 500 × (9/10) × (19/20) = 500 × (171/200)

SP = 2.5 × 171 = 427.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹427.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b429849f3df804496a2e98dc01f4fca757175ec897a90dd2024e832ce2a963d7.png] 

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹500

First discount (D₁) = 10%

Second discount (D₂) = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 500 × (1 − 10/100) × (1 − 5/100)

⇒ SP = 500 × (90/100) × (95/100)

⇒ SP = 500 × 0.90 × 0.95

⇒ SP = 450 × 0.95

⇒ SP = 450 × (1 − 0.05)

⇒ SP = 450 − 22.50 = 427.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹427.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Single Discount Formula

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are allowed, the equivalent single discount is given by: D = [x + y − (x × y) / 100]%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is always set above Cost Price (CP) to allow for discounts while still maintaining a profit. Discounts are always calculated on MP, whereas Profit or Loss is calculated on CP.

Successive Percentage Changes

When any value undergoes multiple percentage changes successively, the final value can be found directly by multiplying the base value with the successive compounding factors: Final Value = Base Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100).

questions.question: A mango juice is made by mixing water and mango concentrate in the ratio 9 : 7. If x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate is mixed in 160 litres of mango juice, then the new ratio becomes 13 : 14. What is the quantity of the new mango juice (in litres)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Water = 160 × (9/16) = 90 L, Initial Mango = 160 × (7/16) = 70 L.

After adding x L water and 3x L mango concentrate, the ratio becomes 13 : 14.

⇒ (90 + x) / (70 + 3x) = 13 / 14

⇒ 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x ⇒ 25x = 350 ⇒ x = 14.

Total new quantity = Initial + Added = 160 + x + 3x = 160 + 4(14) = 216 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a6f67128abfed30430633093a28bd334805628b9214b505d2d0418771f3cc9f.png] 

**Given:**

Total volume of initial mango juice = 160 litres

Ratio of water to mango concentrate = 9 : 7

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quantity of water initially = (9 / 16) × 160 = 90 litres

⇒ Quantity of mango concentrate initially = (7 / 16) × 160 = 70 litres

After adding x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate:

⇒ New quantity of water = (90 + x) litres

⇒ New quantity of mango concentrate = (70 + 3x) litres

According to the given condition, the new ratio is 13 : 14.

⇒ (90 + x) / (70 + 3x) = 13 / 14

⇒ 14 × (90 + x) = 13 × (70 + 3x)

⇒ 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x

⇒ 39x − 14x = 1260 − 910

⇒ 25x = 350

⇒ x = 14

Total new quantity of mango juice = Initial quantity + Added quantities

⇒ Total new quantity = 160 + x + 3x = 160 + 4x

⇒ Total new quantity = 160 + 4 × 14

⇒ Total new quantity = 160 + 56 = 216 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixtures and Ratios

A ratio compares two quantities by division, written as a:b. In mixture problems, always separate the mixture into individual quantitative parts (like litres) before adding or removing components to find the new ratio.

Cross-Multiplication Method

When equating two fractions to form a proportion like a/b = c/d, cross-multiplication states that a × d = b × c. This fundamental property simplifies equations involving two variables in ratio format.

Addition to Mixtures

If distinct quantities are added to an existing compound, the total capacity increases by the sum of all individual additions. New Total Volume = Old Total Volume + Added W + Added M.
</p

questions.question: Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Part of the tank filled by P, Q and R in 3 hours = 3/4

Remaining part of the tank = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

Q and R fill 1/4 part in 2 hours → they can fill the full tank in 8 hours.

Efficiency of P = Total efficiency − Efficiency of (Q + R) = (1/4) − (1/8) = 1/8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (P + Q + R) to fill the tank together = 4 hours

Time taken by (Q + R) to fill the remaining tank after 3 hours = 2 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work completed by (P + Q + R) in 3 hours = 3/4

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

⇒ Time taken by (Q + R) to fill the complete tank = 2 × 4 = 8 hours

 
 

 **Pipes**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P + Q + R
 4
 8
 2
 
 

 Q + R
 8
 1
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of P = Efficiency of (P + Q + R) − Efficiency of (Q + R)

⇒ Efficiency of P = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time taken by P alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of P

⇒ Time taken by P alone = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled by the pipe in 1 hour is 1/x.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Fractional Work

If a/b part of a work is completed in T days, then the total work will be completed in T × (b/a) days.
</p
